mainTopic: Sources and punishments for people who may not do the עבודה: אונן, sitting, בעל מום, מעילה, and a זר who served
overview: The גמרא goes through a ברייתא that lists people who may not do the עבודה in the מקדש. For each one it finds a source and asks how serious the punishment is. It finishes the פסוק about an ערל. It learns the אונן by inference from the כהן גדול's פסוק, and רבא explains why a גזרה שוה cannot give the אונן מיתה. A sitting כהן is disqualified because he was chosen 'to stand and serve.' For a בעל מום and for deliberate מעילה, רבי gives מיתה through word-links: for the בעל מום the source ends up being a טמא ששימש. The רבנן use the word ״בּוֹ״ to limit death and give only an אזהרה. For a זר who served, רבי ישמעאל says death בידי שמים, רבי עקיבא says סקילה, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי says חנק. The גמרא explains the roots of these disputes and settles a contradiction about רבי עקיבא's view. Then the פרק אלו הן הנשרפין ends.

steps.title: End of the verse that disqualifies an uncircumcised כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק in יחזקאל that forbids an ערל from entering the מקדש to serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And one uncircumcised in flesh shall not enter My Sanctuary."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the source it began earlier: the פסוק that teaches an ערל may not serve in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק gives a ban on an ערל serving, but it says nothing about a death penalty. That is why the ערל belongs on the list of people who are disqualified but not punished with מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man
My Sanctuary (the בית המקדש)
To serve Me

phrases.english: "And one uncircumcised in flesh shall not enter
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:9

phrases.english: My Sanctuary (to serve Me)."
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but the corrected text leaves it out. It isn't in the פסוק itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעֶרֶל בָּשָׂר לֹא יָבוֹא אֶל מִקְדָּשִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source for ערל that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: An ערל is disqualified from the עבודה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a mourner may not serve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that an אונן is disqualified from the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אונן, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next person on the list, the אונן, and asks for a source. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן is someone whose close relative died that day. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that such a כהן may not serve.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day a close relative died (before burial)
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: An acute mourner, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: The question is how we know an אונן כהן may not do the עבודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ערל to the next case on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that an אונן is disqualified from the עבודה.

steps.title: Learning the mourner from the High Priest's verse
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק about the כהן גדול. Since he does not leave the מקדש and does not profane it, we infer that an ordinary כהן who does not leave does profane it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out, and he shall not profane the Sanctuary of his God." This implies that another כהן who did not go out has profaned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about a כהן גדול whose relative died. That פסוק says he may stay and serve. From this we infer that a regular כהן who stays and serves while an אונן has profaned the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only directly talks about the כהן גדול, who is allowed to serve as an אונן. The rule for an ordinary כהן is learned by reading it the other way around ('הא אחר'). It is an inference, not an open statement, and that point becomes important in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall not profane
This implies that another (an ordinary כהן)
He has profaned

phrases.english: As it is written: "And from the Sanctuary he shall not go out,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:12. This is about a כהן גדול whose relative died.

phrases.english: and he shall not profane the Sanctuary of his God."
This implies that another who did not go out has profaned it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ordinary כהן אונן is disqualified, learned by inference from the כהן גדול's פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: The כהן גדול here is the one who is ALLOWED to serve as an אונן. The ban on an ordinary כהן comes only from the opposite reading of that פסוק.

steps.title: רב אדא: learn the death penalty from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא suggests a גזרה שוה. The word 'חילול' appears by the אונן and also by an impure כהן eating תרומה. Since that case carries מיתה, the אונן should too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא said to רבא: Let us learn 'profaning' from 'profaning' by תרומה. Just as there the punishment is death, so too here the punishment is death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא challenges putting the אונן on the list of people with no death penalty. He suggests using a גזרה שוה to give the אונן מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By a טמא כהן eating תרומה, the תורה says 'ומתו בו כי יחללוהו', which means death for profaning. Since our case also uses a form of 'חילול', the same word should carry the same punishment. If so, the אונן would be liable to מיתה, which goes against the list.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us learn (derive)
Profaning or desecration
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Death (here, at the hand of Heaven)

phrases.english: Rav Adda said to Rava:
And let us derive "profaning" from "profaning" stated about תרומה,
phrases.notes: When an impure כהן eats תרומה, the פסוק says 'ומתו בו כי יחללוהו' (ויקרא 22:9).

phrases.english: just as there it is punishable by death,
so too here it is punishable by death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא לְרָבָא: וְנֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that an אונן has no death penalty, using the word חילול from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing the אונן among those who serve without being liable to death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'חילול' appears by תרומה, where the punishment is death. A גזרה שוה should carry death over to the אונן.

steps.title: רבא: something learned by inference cannot make a גזרה שוה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that 'חילול' is not written directly about the ordinary כהן אונן. It is only implied from the כהן גדול's פסוק, and a דבר הבא מן הכלל cannot be used for a גזרה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it written about him directly? It comes by inference. It is a matter that comes from an inference, and any matter that comes from an inference is not used for a גזרה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the גזרה שוה. The word 'profane' was never openly said about the ordinary כהן אונן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה links two places where the same word is actually written. Here the ordinary כהן's 'חילול' was only reached by reading the כהן גדול's פסוק in reverse. So it is a דבר הבא מן הכלל, which cannot serve as one side of a גזרה שוה. That is why the אונן stays disqualified, but with no death penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: About itself, directly
It comes by inference
A matter derived only by implication
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: An ordinary כהן אונן is disqualified from the עבודה, learned by inference from the כהן גדול. Because it is only an inference (דבר הבא מן הכלל), we cannot use a גזרה שוה with תרומה to give him מיתה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a general rule for learning from the תורה: a גזרה שוה needs a word that is actually written about the case, not one that is only implied.

phrases.english: Is it written about it itself?
phrases.notes: Is 'profaning' written openly about the ordinary כהן אונן?

phrases.english: It comes by inference.
So it is a matter that comes from an inference,
and any matter that comes from an inference,
we do not derive it by a verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the method: shows the גזרה שוה cannot be applied here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The shared word 'חילול' should carry death from תרומה to the אונן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אונן's 'חילול' is only implied, so it cannot form a גזרה שוה. The אונן is disqualified but not liable to מיתה.

steps.title: Source that a sitting כהן is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a כהן who serves while sitting is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who serves while sitting: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item on the ברייתא's list and asks for the source that a כהן serving while sitting is disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as it asked for sources for the ערל and the אונן, the גמרא now wants a פסוק showing that sitting during the עבודה disqualifies it. This line opens a new item on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is sitting (a כהן serving while seated)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: One who is sitting, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: A כהן doing the עבודה while seated, the next item on the ברייתא's list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the אונן to the next disqualified case in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that sitting disqualifies a כהן's service.

steps.title: Chosen to stand, not to sit
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב נחמן cites the פסוק that the כהן was chosen 'to stand and serve', which excludes sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: the פסוק says, 'For ה׳ your G-d chose him from all your tribes to stand and serve.' I chose him for standing, not for sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that describes the כהן's job as 'standing to serve.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'to stand' (לעמוד) defines the way the כהן was chosen to serve. So service done while sitting is outside what he was chosen for, and it is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: To stand and serve
I chose him
Standing

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
The verse states:
"For him the Lord your God has chosen
phrases.notes: דברים 18:5

phrases.english: from all your tribes, to stand and serve."
For standing I chose him, and not for sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 18:5, 'לעמוד לשרת': the כהן was chosen to serve standing, so sitting disqualifies.

steps.title: Blemished כהן: death or only a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא records a מחלוקת: רבי says a בעל מום who serves gets מיתה, and חכמים say it is only an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A blemished כהן who serves: רבי says he gets death, and the Sages say he has only violated a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes its next case, the בעל מום, along with a disagreement about his punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is not whether he is disqualified but how serious the punishment is. רבי says מיתה בידי שמים, and חכמים say it is only a plain לאו. This sets up the next question about רבי's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish
Death (at the hand of Heaven)
A warning; a plain prohibition

phrases.english: A blemished priest:
Rabbi says: with death,
and the Sages say: with a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי says a serving בעל מום gets מיתה, and חכמים say only an אזהרה.

steps.title: Why does רבי say death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source רבי uses to give the בעל מום the death penalty. This line sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain לאו is clear from the פסוק. The new part that needs a source is רבי's harsher punishment of מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי's view in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי's source for מיתה for a serving בעל מום.

steps.title: גזרה שוה of חילול from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from the word חילול: it appears by the בעל מום and by a טמא כהן eating תרומה, which carries מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'But he shall not come to the curtain...' (and the פסוק continues 'he shall not profane My holy places'). רבי learns 'profaning' from 'profaning' by תרומה. Just as there the punishment is death, so too here it is death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי links the בעל מום to the טמא כהן who eats תרומה, through the shared word חילול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of the בעל מום uses the word חילול, and so does the פסוק of a טמא eating תרומה. Since that case is punished with מיתה, the גזרה שוה carries מיתה over to the בעל מום.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain in the מקדש
Profaning; desecration
The כהן's holy portion of produce
Just as there... so too here

phrases.english: As it is written:
"But he shall not come to the curtain, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:23. The 'etc.' covers the end of the פסוק, 'he shall not profane My holy places'.

phrases.english: And he derives 'profaning,' 'profaning,' from teruma.
Just as there it is with death,
so too here it is with death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה of חילול from a טמא eating תרומה, which carries מיתה.

steps.title: Why not learn from נותר, which gives כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: חילול also appears by נותר, so why not learn from there and give כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us instead learn 'profaning' from 'profaning' by נותר: just as there the punishment is כרת, so too here it should be כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the word חילול appears in another place too, and that place would give a different punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה works by a shared word, but חילול appears both by תרומה (מיתה) and by נותר (כרת). Why did רבי pick תרומה over נותר?

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
And let us derive

phrases.english: But let us derive 'profaning,' 'profaning,' from notar:
phrases.notes: The פסוק about eating נותר also uses the word 'profaned' (ויקרא 19:8).

phrases.english: just as there it is with karet,
so too here it is with karet?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which source the גזרה שוה of step 10 should come from.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's choice of תרומה as the source of the גזרה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears by נותר, which would give כרת instead of מיתה.

steps.title: תרומה is the closer match
steps.stepSummary: It makes more sense to learn from תרומה, because both cases involve a flaw in the person's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is more reasonable that he should learn from תרומה, since that learns a flaw in the body from a flaw in the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי's choice by pointing to a strong likeness between the בעל מום and the טמא eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the blemish and the טומאה are flaws in the כהן himself. נותר is a problem with the meat, not with the person. So תרומה is the more fitting source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is more reasonable
A flaw in the person's body
Since; because

phrases.english: It is reasonable that he should derive from teruma,
since it is a bodily flaw from a bodily flaw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the source with the closer likeness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources are equal, so נותר (כרת) could be used just as well.
steps.terutzMaskana: תרומה fits better because both cases involve a flaw in the person's body.

steps.title: On the contrary, נותר has more in common
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: נותר shares more features with the בעל מום's service, namely קודש, inside the מקדש, פיגול, and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from נותר, since they share these features: holy offerings, inside the מקדש, פיגול, and נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around and lists several ways that נותר is more like the בעל מום's service than תרומה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל מום's service and נותר both deal with קדשים, both happen inside the מקדש, and both can involve the rules of פיגול and נותר. תרומה has none of these, so נותר has more points in common. The next step answers this by finding a source that matches on every point.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Holy sacrificial matters
Inside the מקדש
An offering ruined by a wrong intention about its time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'פיגול ונותר' here as a new topic. These are just the last items in a short memory list of likenesses between the בעל מום's service and נותר.

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should derive from notar,
since they share: sacred matters, inside,
piggul and notar.
phrases.notes: These are short memory words. Each one is a feature that both cases share and תרומה does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12 by counting more likenesses to נותר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תרומה is the better source because both involve a bodily flaw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נותר shares four features (קודש, פנים, פיגול, נותר) with the בעל מום's service, against only one shared feature with תרומה.

steps.title: רבי learns from an impure כהן who served
steps.stepSummary: רבי's real source is not תרומה or נותר. It is a טמא ששימש, an impure כהן who did the עבודה. That case matches the בעל מום in every feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי learns it from an impure כהן who served. He learns a bodily flaw from a bodily flaw. He learns a case of holy things, done inside the מקדש, where פיגול and נותר apply, from a case of holy things, done inside, where פיגול and נותר apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the push-back from step 13 by switching רבי's source to a better match: a טמא כהן who did the עבודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked why we learn from תרומה and not from נותר. Each source matched only some features. A טמא ששימש matches all of them: it has a flaw in the person's body, like תרומה, and it involves קודש, inside the מקדש, with פיגול and נותר, like נותר. So it is the best source, and it carries מיתה.

keyTerms.meaning: An impure כהן who performed the Temple service
A disqualification in the person's own body
Inside, meaning within the מקדש
A קרבן spoiled by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten

phrases.english: Rather, he derives it from an impure kohen who served.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי, and the case he is learning is the בעל מום who did the עבודה.

phrases.english: A bodily disqualification from a bodily disqualification,
sacred, inside, piggul and notar
from sacred, inside, piggul and notar.
phrases.notes: These are the same four features step 13 listed for נותר. Now one source has all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 13 by replacing the source with one that matches on every feature
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the source with a better one that combines both sets of shared features
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי learns from תרומה, or perhaps from נותר, and each one matches only partly
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי learns from a טמא ששימש, which matches the בעל מום on bodily flaw and on קודש, פנים, פיגול and נותר, so the punishment is מיתה

steps.title: The רבנן exclude a בעל מום with the word ״בּוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that a בעל מום who served gets only an אזהרה. The פסוק says ״בּוֹ״, which limits death to its own case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? The פסוק says ״בּוֹ״, "because of it," and not because of a בעל מום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the reason of the רבנן, who disagree with רבי about the בעל מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that gives death says ״וּמֵתוּ בוֹ״, "and die because of it." The רבנן read the extra word ״בּוֹ״ as a limit: death applies to this case only. So any comparison that would give death to a בעל מום is blocked.

keyTerms.meaning: "Because of it": a word read as limiting the law to one case
A כהן with a physical blemish
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: And the Rabbis? The verse says: "Because of it,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:9

phrases.english: and not a blemished kohen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing רבי's source, the גמרא explains the opposing view of the רבנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the רבנן give only an אזהרה to a בעל מום who served?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״בּוֹ״ limits death to its own case and excludes a בעל מום
steps.whatToRemember: For the בעל מום who served, רבי learns מיתה from a טמא ששימש. The רבנן use ״בּוֹ״ to limit death and give only an אזהרה.

steps.title: New case: deliberately misusing holy property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא moves on to someone who deliberately commits מעילה. רבי says he gets מיתה, and the חכמים say only an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deliberately misused holy property: רבי says he is punished with death, and the חכמים say he has only violated a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next case in the ברייתא, which has the same disagreement between רבי and the חכמים. This sets up a new round of "what is the reason."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic changes from the בעל מום to מעילה, but the argument has the same shape: רבי says מיתה, the חכמים say אזהרה. Next the גמרא will ask for each side's reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Acted on purpose, deliberately
Using הקדש, holy property, for one's own benefit
A warning, a plain prohibition with no death penalty
The Sages

phrases.english: One who intentionally committed misuse of holy property:
Rabbi says: with death,
phrases.notes: He means death at the hands of Heaven, the same as in the earlier cases.

phrases.english: and the Sages say: with a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deliberate מעילה: רבי says מיתה בידי שמים, the חכמים say only an אזהרה

steps.title: What is רבי's reason for misuse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי gives death for deliberate מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי's source. This sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not clearly say that מעילה carries death, so רבי must be learning it from somewhere. The גמרא wants to know where.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי's ruling in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי's ruling that deliberate מעילה carries מיתה

steps.title: רבי learns "חטא" from "חטא" by תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that רבי makes a גזירה שוה. The word חטא appears by מעילה and also by תרומה. Since תרומה carries מיתה, so does מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי learns "חטא" here from "חטא" by תרומה. Just as there the punishment is death, so too here the punishment is death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question by showing that רבי uses a word-link, a גזירה שוה, between מעילה and תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about מעילה uses the word חטא, and so does the פסוק about a טמא כהן eating תרומה. Because the same word appears in both, we carry the punishment over. תרומה has מיתה, so מעילה gets מיתה too.

keyTerms.meaning: "Sin": the shared word that links the two cases
He learns or derives one case from another
"Just as there, so too here": the standard formula for carrying a law across

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: גָּמַר חֵטְא חֵטְא מִתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said: He derives "sin" "sin" from terumah.
phrases.notes: The word appears in ויקרא 5:15 about מעילה and in ויקרא 22:9 about תרומה.

phrases.english: Just as there, it is with death,
so too here, it is with death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: גָּמַר חֵטְא חֵטְא מִתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of the word חטא links מעילה to תרומה, which carries מיתה

steps.title: The רבנן exclude מעילה with the word ״בּוֹ״
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן again use ״בּוֹ״ from the תרומה פסוק. Death applies to that case only and not to מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: the פסוק says ״בּוֹ״, "because of it." Because of it there is death, and not for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's reason: the same limiting word ״בּוֹ״ blocks רבי's comparison to תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״בּוֹ״ appears in the תרומה פסוק itself. For the רבנן, it limits death to תרומה only. So even with the word-link of חטא, the death penalty cannot be carried over to מעילה, and only an אזהרה remains.
steps.whatToRemember: In both cases, the בעל מום and מעילה, רבי learns מיתה by comparing to another case. Both times the רבנן use the limiting word ״בּוֹ״ to block the comparison and give only an אזהרה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: the verse says "because of it,"
"because of it," and not for misuse of holy property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי's source in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the רבנן give only an אזהרה for deliberate מעילה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״בּוֹ״ in the תרומה פסוק limits death to תרומה and excludes מעילה

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a non-priest who served dies at the hand of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses a גזירה שוה from 'הקרב' to rule that a זר who served in the מקדש gets מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a non-priest who served in the Temple, a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says the פסוק here says 'the non-priest who comes near shall be put to death', and another פסוק says 'anyone who comes near the משכן of ה׳ shall die'. Just as there it means death by Heaven, so too here it means death by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case on the list, a זר who did the עבודה. It quotes a ברייתא, starting with רבי ישמעאל's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the word 'הקרב', meaning one who comes near. The second פסוק clearly means death בידי שמים, so רבי ישמעאל carries that over to the זר. This means no בית דין carries out the death.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-כהן
Death at the hand of Heaven, not by בית דין
Here / there: the two פסוקים being compared

phrases.english: A non-priest who served in the Temple:
phrases.notes: These are the words from the list being discussed. Now the גמרא explains this case.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yishmael says:
It says here: 'And the non-priest who comes near shall be put to death',
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:7

phrases.english: and it says there

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל הַקָּרֵב הַקָּרֵב אֶל מִשְׁכָּן ה׳ יָמוּת״.
phrases.english: 'Anyone who comes near, who comes near the Tabernacle of ה׳, shall die.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:28

phrases.english: Just as there it is by the hand of Heaven,
so too here it is by the hand of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָר שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ בְּמִקְדָּשׁ: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of מעילה to the next case on the list, a זר who served.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, a זר who served gets מיתה בידי שמים, learned from 'הקרב' in במדבר 17:28.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the non-priest is stoned, like the false prophet
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns 'יומת' from 'יומת' by the false נביא, so the זר gets סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says the פסוק here says 'the non-priest who comes near shall be put to death', and the פסוק there says 'that prophet or that dreamer of a dream shall be put to death'. Just as there it is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל. He compares the זר to a different פסוק, the one about a false נביא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא connects the זר to the נביא through the word 'יומת', which appears in both פסוקים. A נביא who leads people to עבודה זרה is stoned, so the זר is stoned too. This makes the death a בית דין punishment, the opposite of רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, a death penalty carried out by בית דין
'Shall be put to death', which suggests death by בית דין
A dreamer of a dream: a false prophet type

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
It says here: 'And the non-priest who comes near shall be put to death',
and it says there

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהַנָּבִיא הַהוּא אוֹ חֹלֵם הַחֲלוֹם הַהוּא יוּמָת״.
phrases.english: 'And that prophet or that dreamer of a dream shall be put to death.'
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6

phrases.english: Just as there it is by stoning,
so too here it is by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second view in the same ברייתא, arguing with רבי ישמעאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a זר who served gets סקילה, learned from the false נביא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: the זר is strangled
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי makes the same comparison to the נביא, but holds the נביא gets חנק, so the זר gets חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: just as there it is strangulation, so too here it is strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: A third view in the ברייתא. רבי יוחנן בן נורי agrees with רבי עקיבא's comparison but gives a different death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts the link between the זר and the false נביא. He disagrees about how the נביא himself is killed: he says חנק, not סקילה. So the זר gets חנק too.

keyTerms.meaning: Strangulation, a בית דין death penalty

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
Just as there it is by strangulation,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the same פסוק about the false נביא that רבי עקיבא used.

phrases.english: so too here it is by strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: מָה לְהַלָּן בְּחֶנֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי עקיבא's comparison but changes the result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, a זר who served gets חנק, since the false נביא gets חנק.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא are arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one brought a different גזירה שוה. The גמרא wants to know why each one thought his own comparison was better.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? It asks for the root of an argument

phrases.english: About what do they disagree,
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the views in steps 20 and 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why each תנא chose his own גזירה שוה over the other's.

steps.title: Matching words versus matching people
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא wants the exact same word, 'יומת' with 'יומת'. רבי ישמעאל wants the same kind of person, an ordinary person compared to an ordinary person, not to a נביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds we learn 'יומת' from 'יומת', and not 'יומת' from 'ימות'. רבי ישמעאל holds we learn a הדיוט from a הדיוט, and not a הדיוט from a נביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: each side has a different rule for which comparison is stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא says a closer match in wording wins, and 'יומת' matches 'יומת' exactly while 'ימות' does not. רבי ישמעאל says a closer match in the type of person wins. The זר is an ordinary person, like the person who comes near the משכן, not like a נביא.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn or derive one case from another
'Shall die', which suggests death בידי שמים
An ordinary person, not a נביא

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two words carefully: יוּמָת means 'shall be put to death' and is used for the זר and the נביא. יָמוּת means 'shall die' and is used for the one who comes near the משכן. They look almost the same.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
We learn 'shall be put to death' from 'shall be put to death',
and we do not learn 'shall be put to death' from 'shall die'.
And Rabbi Yishmael holds:
We learn an ordinary person from an ordinary person,
and we do not learn an ordinary person from a prophet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא puts exact wording first. רבי ישמעאל puts a similar kind of person first.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: a prophet who led people astray is just an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's point. Once the נביא led people to עבודה זרה, he is the most ordinary person there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? Once he led people astray, there is no one more ordinary than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא handles רבי ישמעאל's argument that we should not compare an ordinary person to a נביא, and gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's argument only works if the false נביא still counts as a נביא. רבי עקיבא says he loses that status the moment he pushes people to עבודה זרה. So comparing the זר to him is comparing ordinary to ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: He led others astray, toward עבודה זרה
A prophet

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking how רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's point about not learning from a נביא.

phrases.english: Once he led people astray,
you have no ordinary person greater than this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי עקיבא against the reasoning that step 24 gave for רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the status of the false נביא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A false נביא is still a נביא, so an ordinary זר cannot be compared to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נביא who led people astray loses his special status and counts as a הדיוט, so the comparison works.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל: same type of person, so the זר gets death בידי שמים. רבי עקיבא: same exact word, so the זר gets סקילה, and the false נביא counts as an ordinary person anyway.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא says סקילה and רבי יוחנן בן נורי says חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the second argument. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both use the same comparison to the false נביא, so their argument cannot be about the comparison. It must be about something else.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי?
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the first argument, the גמרא turns to the second one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What causes רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי to reach different deaths from the same comparison.

steps.title: They follow the argument about a prophet who led people astray
steps.stepSummary: Their argument matches a ברייתא argument: the רבנן say a נביא שהדיח gets סקילה, and רבי שמעון says חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree the same way as רבי שמעון and the רבנן. As a ברייתא teaches: a prophet who led people astray is stoned. רבי שמעון says: strangled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole argument depends on how the false נביא is killed. That is a known argument between רבי שמעון and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא agrees with the רבנן that the נביא gets סקילה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי agrees with רבי שמעון that he gets חנק. Each one then carries his view over to the זר.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument or dispute
A prophet who led others to עבודה זרה

phrases.english: In the argument of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis,
as it was taught: A prophet who led people astray is stoned.
Rabbi Shimon says: by strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא follows the רבנן, so the נביא gets סקילה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי follows רבי שמעון, so the נביא gets חנק.

steps.title: But a משנה quotes רבי עקיבא as saying strangulation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: a משנה has רבי עקיבא saying חנק for the false נביא, not סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: רבי עקיבא says: by strangulation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. A משנה seems to show that רבי עקיבא gives the false נביא חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 placed רבי עקיבא with the רבנן, who say סקילה. If a משנה quotes him as saying חנק, then he is really on רבי שמעון's side. That would contradict the ברייתא, where he gave the זר סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה: introduces a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: But we learned in a משנה:
Rabbi Akiva says: by strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אֲנַן תְּנַן: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בְּחֶנֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא holds the false נביא gets סקילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה quotes רבי עקיבא as saying חנק for the false נביא. That contradicts his ruling of סקילה for the זר, which was learned from the נביא.

steps.title: Two students report רבי עקיבא's view differently
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction about רבי עקיבא is solved: two תנאים disagree about what רבי עקיבא held. The משנה follows רבי שמעון's report, and the ברייתא follows the רבנן's report.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי עקיבא held. The משנה is רבי שמעון's version of רבי עקיבא's opinion. The ברייתא is the רבנן's version of רבי עקיבא's opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from Step 28. It says the משנה and the ברייתא are not really fighting. Each one reports רבי עקיבא's opinion through a different student tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 27 we learned that the רבנן say a נביא שהדיח gets סקילה, and רבי שמעון says חנק. Now the גמרא says both sides claim to follow רבי עקיבא. So the משנה, which quotes רבי עקיבא as saying חנק, is really רבי שמעון's way of reporting him. The ברייתא, which quotes him as saying סקילה, is the רבנן's way of reporting him.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (two sages of the משנה period) who disagree
According to the opinion of; how someone understood another sage's view
Our משנה
A teaching of the תנאים that was left out of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא changed his mind or held two opinions. He held one view. Two different groups remembered and reported that one view differently.
steps.whatToRemember: When two sources quote the same sage in opposite ways, the גמרא can answer "תרי תנאי ואליבא ד...": two later sages disagreed about what that earlier sage really held.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion about the false נביא's death penalty. It saves the earlier answer from Step 27: רבי עקיבא's two reports line up with the two sides of the רבנן and רבי שמעון argument.

phrases.english: These are two תנאים, and they disagree about the opinion of רבי עקיבא.
The משנה is רבי שמעון,
according to how he understood רבי עקיבא.
phrases.notes: That is why the משנה quotes רבי עקיבא as saying חנק, which is רבי שמעון's own view from Step 27.

phrases.english: The ברייתא is the רבנן,
according to how they understood רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 28 by splitting the two reports of רבי עקיבא between two later תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different traditions about one sage (תרי תנאי אליבא דחד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה, where רבי עקיבא says חנק, seems to contradict the claim that the ברייתא's רבנן, who hold סקילה, follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects רבי שמעון's report of רבי עקיבא (חנק). The ברייתא reflects the רבנן's report of רבי עקיבא (סקילה). So there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of those who are burned
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the ninth פרק of סנהדרין, אלו הן הנשרפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, "אלו הן הנשרפין" (These are the ones who are burned).
steps.whatsHappening: This is not part of the argument. It is the traditional line said when we finish a פרק, and it marks the end of the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרק is named after its opening words, "אלו הן הנשרפין." Saying הדרן shows our wish to come back and learn this chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula said when finishing a פרק
Those who are put to death by burning (שריפה)

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"These are the ones who are burned."
phrases.notes: This is the name of the פרק we just finished, taken from its first words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after the last discussion ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק אלו הן הנשרפין is complete.
